title: Tamsin and the Crown
premise: Rosalind Brightwater survives the usurper's court by tasting poison and keeping the ledgers of the Veiled Guild, which trades in impossible things—years, names, second chances. When a prophecy written a century ago surfaces bearing tonight's date and Rosalind's true name, they learn they are the last heir of the covenant that once bound the mortal realm to the fae courts, a pact the usurper broke to seize power. Hunted by both armies and courtiers alike, Rosalind must gather the scattered covenant-stones, confront the fae queen who abandoned their bloodline, and choose between reclaiming a crown they never wanted or forging a new covenant that dissolves royal power entirely. In the end, Rosalind reforges the covenant as an accord among free cities, guilds, and courts—the usurper falls not to armies but to his own name being traded away—and Rosalind walks away from every throne, ledger finally balanced.
about_author: Astrid Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write stories about ordinary people who discover their names in old books, and live in a drafty coastal house full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A night of routine poison-tasting at the usurper's table is interrupted when Guildmaster Corvane shows Rosalind a century-old prophecy book: tonight's date, a taster, a name—Rosalind's birth name, thought buried. The emotional beat is dread blooming into vertigo; the invisible life Rosalind built begins cracking open as the usurper's spymaster starts asking questions about the guild's ledgers.

chapters.title: What the Queen Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the exiled fae queen Ysolde. Fleeing the capital, Rosalind bargains with the Veiled Guild for passage and learns the covenant-stones were pawned during the last war. Ysolde, dying and bitter, reveals Rosalind's bloodline was her price for survival long ago. The beat is fury and grief: inheritance revealed as abandonment, and Rosalind realizing survival itself has been their whole inheritance.

chapters.title: The Price of Stones
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Racing the usurper's armies to the free cities, Rosalind must trade impossible things to recover each covenant-stone—a year of life, the memory of their mother, Corvane's loyalty. Each bargain corrupts someone they love. Climactic beat: Rosalind holds all three stones and understands power's price firsthand, tempted at last to simply take the throne rather than unmake it.

chapters.title: A Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: All POVs converge at the ruined covenant-moor as the armies clash. Rosalind reforges the pact—not restoring the old crown but binding realms to the free cities and guilds, trading away the usurper's claim-name so his own soldiers forget why they follow him. Ysolde's debt is paid in Rosalind's choice to refuse kingship. Final beat: quiet, costly peace; Rosalind closes the ledger on themselves and walks home unnamed.
